say.text: They take the road north to Mosul, where Zengi rules.
Do you hold it against me, Najm?
I hold a new son and a brother's hand. That is enough to travel with.
Zengi received them kindly. He gave them a large fief and took them into his army, in return for the service Ayyub had done him at Tikrit.
In time Ayyub would hold Baalbek for him, as its warden; and after Zengi's death he would become one of the great emirs of Damascus, and Shirkuh would serve Nur ad-Din.
Ayyub was known as a pious and generous man who loved holy company.
